Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(p=397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue is invertible.

First note that \(a_n\neq 396\), because if \(a_n=396\), then \((a_n+1)^2\equiv 0\pmod{397}\), giving

\[
0\equiv a_n\equiv 396\pmod{397},
\]

impossible. Also \(a_0=1\), and from

\[
a_{n+1}\equiv \frac{a_n}{(a_n+1)^2}\pmod{397},
\]

we see \(a_n\neq 0\) for all \(n\). Thus we may define

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Now invert the recurrence:

\[
b_{n+1}\equiv (a_n+1)^2 a_n^{-1}
\equiv a_n+2+a_n^{-1}
\equiv b_n^{-1}+2+b_n.
\]

Therefore,

\[
a_n\equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2(2027).
\]

We have \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Since

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+b_{2026}^{-1}
\equiv 9^{-1}+2+9
\equiv 9^{-1}+11,
\]

and

\[
9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\pmod{397},
\]

we get

\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\pmod{397}.
\]

Thus

\[
b_{2027}\equiv 353+11=364.
\]

Finally,

\[
2(2027)=4054\equiv 84\pmod{397},
\]

so

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84
=279\pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
